newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: "Defectors" say Khmer Rouge funded opposition.
newsitem.headline: "Defectors" say Khmer Rouge funded opposition.

text.p: Ten Cambodians who said they had been undercover Khmer Rouge agents accused opposition leader Sam Rainsy on Saturday of taking secret funds and support from the pariah Maoist movement.
Sam Rainsy is a former finance minister who advocates reconciliation with the Khmer Rouge. He formed the opposition Khmer Nation Party after being expelled from the royalist FUNCINPEC in June 1995.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen met the self-proclaimed defectors before the press conference at his home at which they made their charges.
Their leader, Duong Buntha, said Sam Rainsy met the Khmer Rouge's Khieu Samphan in Thailand before founding the KNP last year.
"We were told to send 16,007 members to join Sam Rainsy's party," he said, reading a prepared statement.
"There was discussion of giving $2 million and Sin Sareth (a Khmer Rouge official)...gave it to Sam Rainsy on July 20, 1995," Duong Buntha said.

Several analysts said there was no concrete evidence to support allegations against the KNP, which was seen by Hun Sen as a dangerous rival for partnership with Cambodia's other co-premier FUNCINPEC's Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

"This is obviously related...to the possibility of the two parties forming a coalition against (Hun Sen's) Cambodian People's Party," said one Westerner. "It is clearly orchestrated by Hun Sen, and there's no doubt about that."
